# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision

The Conservatives present their manifesto as a continuation of economic recovery following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. They highlight falling inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), rising real wages, and returning growth as evidence their plan is working. The party commits to reducing borrowing and debt while maintaining fiscal rules.

## Key Tax Pledges

The centrepiece is cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual saving for average workers. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household basis, with families retaining benefits until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Borders

The manifesto promises a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes, continuing Rwanda deportation flights, and reforming international asylum rules. They claim small boat arrivals fell by one-third last year and Albanian arrivals dropped 90%.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, described as the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The party commits to continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent modernisation, and strengthening NATO partnerships.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The manifesto promises 8,000 additional neighbourhood police officers, 40 new hospitals by 2030, and expanded mental health support in schools.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The target is 1.6 million new homes, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Transport investment of £36 billion from HS2 savings would fund local projects, including £8.3 billion for road repairs.

## Energy and Environment

The party commits to net zero by 2050 through a "pragmatic" approach, including annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, trebling offshore wind capacity, and expanding nuclear power with Small Modular Reactors. They promise no new green levies on household bills.

## Young People

A mandatory National Service programme would offer 18-year-olds either military placements or community volunteering. Education reforms include the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education, 100,000 new apprenticeships, and mobile phone bans in schools.
